cards.explanation: The answer is cutting themselves or shaving their foreheads. Moses says Israel must not cut themselves or shave their foreheads on behalf of the dead (Deuteronomy 14:1). It's the very first instruction in the chapter, right after he calls them sons of the LORD their God. Loss is heavy, friends, and I think that's a tender place for a rule to land.

The answer is that they are a people holy to the LORD. Moses ties the rule straight to who they are: "…for you are a people holy to the LORD your God." (Deuteronomy 14:2) Back in verse 1 he had just called them sons of the LORD their God. I think that's the heart of it, friends. Whose they are shapes what they do.

The answer is True. It's right there: "The LORD has chosen you to be a people for His prized possession out of all the peoples on the face of the earth." (Deuteronomy 14:2) Prized possession, friends. I know a little about being picked up out of a bin of bargains, so that line gets me right in the apron.

The answer is a split hoof and chewing the cud. Two checks, and the animal has to pass both. Moses says, "You may eat any animal that has a split hoof divided in two and that chews the cud." (Deuteronomy 14:6) One out of two doesn't get through the door. He's about to show us exactly that.

The answer is False. The camel, the rabbit and the rock badger chew the cud, but they don't have a divided hoof. Moses calls them unclean for Israel (Deuteronomy 14:7). One check passed and one missed means they stay off the list. Picture rolling up to a job interview in a sharp jacket and no pants, friends, because dressed halfway is not dressed.

The answer is that the pig does not chew the cud. The pig passes the hoof check, since it has a divided hoof. But Moses says it does not chew the cud, so it is unclean for Israel (Deuteronomy 14:8). That second check is the one it misses.

The answer is True. Moses gives two separate rules about the pig: "You must not eat its meat or touch its carcass." (Deuteronomy 14:8) One is about eating the meat. The other is about touching the carcass. So the rule reaches past the dinner table, friends.

The answer is scales. Fins and scales, both. Moses says, "Of all the creatures that live in the water, you may eat anything with fins and scales…" (Deuteronomy 14:9) Anything in the water without fins and scales is unclean for them. One test for the whole sea.

The answer is False. Moses says, "All flying insects are unclean for you; they may not be eaten." (Deuteronomy 14:19) Not one bug with wings gets a pass, friends. Mosquito, moth, whatever's buzzing around your porch light: all off the menu. Honestly, my ovens stay bug free, so I've never had to worry.

The answer is foreigner. Moses says, "You are not to eat any carcass; you may give it to the foreigner residing within your gates, and he may eat it, or you may sell it to a foreigner." (Deuteronomy 14:21) So it goes either way, given or sold. Nothing in that line says to toss it out.

The answer is a tenth. Moses says, "You must be sure to set aside a tenth of all the produce brought forth each year from your fields." (Deuteronomy 14:22) It's a share of all of it, and it's every year. Ten cookies on the tray, one set aside. That's the picture, friends.

The answer is to eat it before the LORD. Moses says Israel is to eat that tenth in the LORD's presence, at the place He will choose as a dwelling for His Name (Deuteronomy 14:23). The grain, the new wine and oil, and the firstborn of the herds and flocks all go on that table. This tithe comes with a seat before the LORD.

The answer is to fear the LORD their God always. Moses gives the reason himself: "…so that you may learn to fear the LORD your God always." (Deuteronomy 14:23) The eating happens in His presence, and the learning comes with it. Always, friends, not just on feast days.

The answer is True. If the place is too far to carry what the LORD has blessed them with, Moses says they can exchange it for money, take the money in hand, and go to the place the LORD will choose (Deuteronomy 14:24, 25). A lighter load for the road, friends.

The answer is False. It isn't only cattle and sheep. Moses says, "…you may spend the money on anything you desire: cattle, sheep, wine, strong drink, or anything you wish." (Deuteronomy 14:26) Cattle and sheep are just the start of the list. Anything you wish, friends.

The answer is rejoice. Moses says, "You are to feast there in the presence of the LORD your God and rejoice with your household." (Deuteronomy 14:26) A feast, a family and gladness, all in one verse. I love a sermon with a party in it.

The answer is that the Levite has no portion or inheritance. That's the reason Moses gives: "…since he has no portion or inheritance among you." (Deuteronomy 14:27) He tells Israel not to neglect the Levite within their gates, and this is why. As Moses lays out the feast, someone is still on his mind.

The answer is in their own towns. Moses says, "…bring a tenth of all your produce for that year and lay it up within your gates." (Deuteronomy 14:28) Within their gates means right at home in their own towns. This time the tithe stays close instead of making the trip.

The answer is the foreigner, the fatherless and the widow. Moses says, "…the Levite (because he has no portion or inheritance among you), the foreigner, the fatherless, and the widow within your gates may come and eat and be satisfied." (Deuteronomy 14:29) Everybody gets a seat at that table, friends. I always say the best part of a full batch is a full table.

The answer is True. That's how Moses closes it: "And the LORD your God will bless you in all the work of your hands." (Deuteronomy 14:29) It comes right after the Levite, the foreigner, the fatherless and the widow come to eat and be satisfied. A promise of blessing on all the work of their hands. And the story isn't over, friends, because Moses still has more to say.
